summary: HTTP/2 connection-level metadata reuse causes idempotency header collision and duplicate function invocations across concurrent streams
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observes duplicate external tool/function invocations originating from single logical requests when traffic is sent over HTTP/2. The customer uses a client-side load balancer that opens a small pool of long-lived HTTP/2 connections to our edge-proxy. When multiple concurrent SDK requests share the same connection, the per-request idempotency header appears to be reused/overwritten at the connection level, causing the serving runtime to treat retries as new requests and replay tool calls.

Impact:
- Multiple customers' downstream systems received duplicate webhook/tool invocations (side effects include duplicate DB writes and duplicate job submissions).
- High-severity for Polaris Labs: visible production data duplication on a subset of requests (~0.3% of calls during peak concurrency).

Environment:
- Polaris Labs Dedicated account on prod us-east-1.
- Uses both SDK-Go (v1.8.2) and SDK-TS (v0.9.5) in different services behind a shared Envoy edge-proxy cluster configured for HTTP/2 connection pooling.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Configure two worker services to send concurrent streaming funcall requests over the same client connection pool (mimic concurrency 20+).
2) Instrument idempotency header X-Redwood-Idempotency with short unique tokens generated per logical request.
3) Force an intermittent 502 from a downstream tool service (simulated) to trigger SDK retry logic.
4) Observe downstream tool receives duplicate invocations tied to the same logical request.

Observed behavior:
- Idempotency header value in requests reaching the serving-runtime sometimes does not match the original token generated by the SDK for that logical request; it appears to be overwritten by a header from a different concurrent stream on the same HTTP/2 connection.
- SDK client logs show a single idempotency token emitted per logical request; edge-proxy logs show different token values after pooling/metadata processing.

Expected behavior:
- Idempotency header should be scoped to each logical request/stream and never be mutated by connection-level metadata handling. Retries should reuse the original token and deduplicate server-side tool invocations.

Relevant logs/links:
- Customer-provided pcap and request traces: s3://polaris-prod-traces/2026-03-09/http2-pool-analysis.tar.gz
- Edge-proxy access log excerpts attached to ticket (see comment).
- Partial spike observed in serving-runtime trace id 20260309-22a.

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Disable HTTP/2 connection pooling (set connection: new) on their client-side LB or configure per-stream header isolation (per-connection metadata disabled) to prevent header reuse.
- As an alternative, set the idempotency token in the request body rather than as a connection header (requires application change).

Notes:
- Customer is on Dedicated plan; request classified as P1 due to production side-effects and data duplication.
steps_to_reproduce: Open 20+ concurrent client streams over pooled HTTP/2 connections to edge-proxy
Attach X-Redwood-Idempotency header per logical request
Trigger transient 502 from downstream tool to cause SDK retry
Inspect edge-proxy and serving-runtime logs for header values and duplicate tool invocations
observed_behavior: Idempotency header values differ between SDK emit and serving-runtime receipt
Duplicate tool/webhook invocations observed on retries
Issue only appears under connection pooling + high concurrency
expected_behavior: Server-side dedup prevents duplicate tool invocations on retries
temporary_workaround: Disable HTTP/2 pooling on client LB
Send idempotency token in request body instead of header
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Sara Nguyen): Acknowledged. Reproduced with a small dev harness that opens pooled HTTP/2 connections; adding Eng and SRE for triage.

2026-03-10 11:03 - SRE (Diego Torres): Edge-proxy config shows a custom callout that copies per-stream headers into connection-level metadata for performance. Suspect copy path is causing header mutation on reuse.

2026-03-10 14:21 - Customer (Polaris Support): We applied the suggested workaround (disable pooling) and duplicates stopped within 30 minutes. We can keep pooled connections disabled but would prefer a platform-side fix.

2026-03-11 08:37 - Eng (Nina Patel): Created initial repro and confirmed that Envoy metadata-to-header rewrite race condition can occur when callout cache is used. Drafting a patch to ensure per-stream header isolation. Reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/789
2026-03-12 10:01 - Support (Sara Nguyen): Customer notified that mitigation is available and patch is in review. Scheduled follow-up to validate once patch is rolled to prod for Dedicated customers.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: edge-proxy/Envoy metadata caching layer treats idempotency header as connection-scoped when callouts are enabled, leading to other streams reusing the last-seen value.
Confirmed repro: local harness using Envoy with metadata cache reproduces header overwrite under high concurrency.
serving-runtime observed request IDs mapping show mismatched idempotency tokens vs SDK logs; correlation points to edge-proxy rewrite path.
Potentially impacted SDKs: SDK-Go header injection + HTTP/2 client pooling; SDK-TS similar when run behind same LB patterns.
Risk: Broad — any customers using HTTP/2 pooling with per-request idempotency headers are at risk of duplicates until patched.
mitigation_and_next_steps: Short term: Recommend customers disable HTTP/2 pooling or move idempotency into body; support notified Polaris that disabling pooling mitigated issue.
Medium term: Edge-proxy patch to guarantee per-stream header isolation (PR #789) — ensure metadata-to-header callout is per-stream and not cached at connection level.
Long term: SDK change to attach idempotency tokens in a manner that cannot be altered by connection-level middleware (SDK-Go PR #412), plus a test harness for pooled HTTP/2 scenarios.
SRE rollout plan: staged deploy to Dedicated edge clusters with canary in us-east-1, monitor duplicate-funcall metric and 5xx rates for 24h.
resolution: Mitigation applied: customer workaround accepted (pooling disabled). Edge-proxy patch (https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/789) under review and SDK change (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/412) queued. After PRs merge, target rollout to Dedicated prod in 72h and re-run regression tests. Follow-up ticket assigned to INT-4422 for rollout coordination.
notes_for_postmortem: Include reproduction steps for HTTP/2 pooling in postmortem
Quantify customer impact and list customers that had similar LB patterns
Recommend documentation update: SDK guidance for idempotency header placement when using HTTP/2 pools
